title: How to Get Paid to Care for a Family Member in Missouri (CDS, Step by Step)
short_title: How to get paid to care for a family member in Missouri
description: If someone you love has Missouri Medicaid and needs help at home, they may be able to choose you as their paid caregiver through Consumer Directed Services (CDS). Here is the whole path, start to finish: who can be paid, the 8 steps, and how caregiver pay works.
end: Take the 2-minute check, or give us a call.

parts.head: How to get paid to care for a family member in Missouri
parts.sub: Start to finish, step by step
parts.text: If someone you love has Missouri Medicaid and needs help at home, you may be able to get paid to care for them. It's called Consumer Directed Services, or CDS. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS, and in the next few minutes I'll walk you through how it works, start to finish.

parts.head: You choose your caregiver
parts.sub: Medicaid pays them. No cost to you.
parts.text: In CDS, the person who needs care chooses their own caregiver. Often it's someone they already know and trust: an adult son or daughter, a grandchild, a friend, or the neighbor who already helps. Medicaid pays the caregiver, and there's no cost to the person receiving care.

parts.head: Who can be paid
parts.sub: Not a spouse. Not a guardian or conservator.
parts.text: Almost anyone they trust can be the paid caregiver, as long as they're eighteen or older, legally able to work in the US, and pass the state's background screening. Two people can't be paid: a spouse, and a court-appointed guardian or conservator. That's a Missouri rule, not ours.

parts.head: The person receiving care stays in charge
parts.sub: They choose, set the schedule, say what help they need
parts.text: One more rule matters. The person receiving care has to direct their own care: choose the caregiver, set the schedule, and say what help they need. Family can help them think it through, but the decisions are theirs.

parts.head: Check that CDS fits
parts.sub: Missouri Medicaid (MO HealthNet) + a need for help at home
parts.text: Here's the whole path, in order. Step one: check that CDS fits. You need Missouri Medicaid, also called MO HealthNet, and a need for help with daily living. Our two-minute check at caringcds.com asks the five questions that matter, or call us and we'll do it with you on the phone.

parts.head: Referral and state assessment
parts.sub: Your plan of care: the tasks and the hours
parts.text: Step two: the state assessment. We refer you to the state, or you can refer yourself. The state then contacts you to set up an assessment of the help you need. The result is your plan of care: the tasks your caregiver is paid for, and how many hours. Switching from another CDS agency? There's no new assessment. Your hours move with you.

parts.head: Enroll with us
parts.sub: One signing packet, on your phone or on paper
parts.text: Step three: enroll with us. It's one signing packet, on your phone or on paper, whichever you prefer.

parts.head: Become the employer, on paper
parts.sub: We do both tax enrollments for you
parts.text: Step four: become the employer, on paper. In CDS, the caregiver works for the person receiving care, not for us, and not for the state. That takes two tax numbers, and we do both enrollments for you. Your part is a few signatures.

parts.head: Choose your caregiver
parts.sub: No one in mind? See local caregivers at findcdscaregivers.com
parts.text: Step five: choose your caregiver. Most families already know who they want. If you don't have anyone, our private caregiver directory, Find CDS Caregivers, lets you see local caregivers' profiles and ask to meet the ones you like. Meeting someone doesn't commit you. You still choose who you hire.

parts.head: Orientation
parts.sub: One honest conversation with a checklist, and we help
parts.text: Step six: orientation. Missouri asks the employer to go over eight topics with the new caregiver. It sounds formal, but it's really one honest conversation with a checklist, and we help you with it.

parts.head: Clocking in (EVV)
parts.sub: Mobile app or the home phone. We do a practice run.
parts.text: Step seven: clocking in. Missouri requires electronic visit verification, so the caregiver clocks in and out with a mobile app, or by calling from the home phone. Before the first shift, our onboarding specialist calls to set it up and do a practice run.

parts.head: The first shift
parts.sub: We handle payroll, taxes and filings
parts.text: Step eight: the first shift. The caregiver works the schedule you set, within your authorized hours, and we handle payroll, taxes and filings. We check in by phone every month, and visit once a year.

parts.head: $15 to $16 an hour, every Thursday
parts.sub: Direct deposit or a pay card. You get a W-2.
parts.text: So how does the caregiver get paid? With us, it's fifteen to sixteen dollars an hour, every Thursday. The pay week runs Sunday through Saturday, the hours are approved early the next week, and pay lands that Thursday by direct deposit or a pay card. Taxes are taken out, and you get a W-2.

parts.head: Only work authorized hours
parts.sub: Hours outside the plan of care can't be paid
parts.text: One tip that saves caregivers money: never work hours that aren't in the plan of care. They can't be paid.

parts.head: Our steps move in days
parts.sub: The state assessment moves at the state's pace
parts.text: How long does it all take? The steps we control move in days. The state assessment moves at the state's pace, which varies by county and season.

We serve twenty-seven counties in southwest Missouri. To see if you qualify, take the two-minute check at caringcds.com, or call us at 417-218-2888, Monday to Friday, nine to four. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS. Thanks for watching.
